source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.16
text: Before seedlings are pulled from the nursery for transplanting, producers should check that they have grown to a healthy standard: seedlings should have developed strong growth of about 3–4 leaves, and be around 20 days old (counting from sowing) before being uprooted. Healthy seedlings should stand about 15–20 cm tall. The manual specifically warns against seedlings that have grown too tall/leggy (about 30–40 cm), illustrating this as an unhealthy, undesirable condition (marked with an X) because overly tall, leggy seedlings are prone to breaking/lodging when pulled and transplanted and establish poorly. Producers are also told to monitor the nursery's germination/establishment rate and manage water depth carefully during the nursery stage so seedlings develop evenly.
